neighboring_unit_entries.title: Density bounds, parity of vanishing, and strict nonvanishing gains
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Uses positivity and parity of central vanishing order to turn extremal density values into explicit nonvanishing proportions, and shows why splitting signs gives a strict mean-order gain that the parity-mixed O-kernel cannot provide.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: A projection argument characterizes when squared sinc is optimal
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Proves the Fredholm minimizer by decomposing any normalized competitor into the solution plus an orthogonal remainder, then shows the constant Fourier factor—and hence squared sinc—is optimal exactly when the kernel average is constant.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Off-diagonal arithmetic makes the Fourier-side density kernel nonconstant; positivity then turns zero density into a band-limited extremal problem whose Fredholm solution improves central nonvanishing bounds.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The resulting proportions are lower bounds under the source's hypotheses, not exact nonvanishing densities.
